deviations: D1: User and PushSubscription are NOT auto-stamped with FleetId by SaveChanges guard. Null FleetId is a legitimate persisted state for customers/superadmin rows. The guard only throws when the entity carries a non-null FleetId that mismatches a non-null current tenant. This is by design and prevents corrupting customer creation in WI-06.

D2: Middleware unit-test approach chosen for Tenancy_Resolution_PrefersJwtClaimThenHeaderThenSubdomain. No probe endpoint was added. The full pipeline integration proof (HealthCheckTests) confirms that the convention-based InvokeAsync(HttpContext, CurrentTenant, TaxiDbContext) DI injection wires correctly at runtime. WI-08 CreateOrder will provide header-based resolution in an endpoint request.

D3: InternalsVisibleTo added to Taxi.Api.csproj for Taxi.Api.Tests. This allows tests to access CurrentTenant (to set FleetId) and TenantResolutionMiddleware (to instantiate directly) while keeping both internal per csharp-style rules. No API surface exposed externally.

D4 (round-2 F1): GuardTenantEntities() extended to cover EntityState.Modified in addition to Added. Auto-stamp (FleetId=Guid.Empty → current tenant) is still Added-only. Modified entities with a FleetId mismatching the current tenant now throw InvalidOperationException, preventing cross-tenant row migration.

D5 (round-2 F2): Added lock-in test Tenancy_QueryFilter_NullTenant_StrictEntityReturnsZeroRows. Seeds an Order via a raw scope, confirms the row exists via IgnoreQueryFilters, then queries via a null-tenant scope and asserts zero rows — proves fail-closed behaviour for strict-filter entities.

D6 (round-2 F3): ICurrentTenant, ITenantEntity, and TenantClaims changed from public to internal. TaxiDbContext changed from public to internal to resolve CS0051 (parameter less accessible than method). Public entity classes implementing internal ITenantEntity compile without issues (C# allows public class to implement internal interface). InternalsVisibleTo already covers the test project.

D7 (round-2 F4): TenantResolutionMiddleware fleet_id claim branch now gated on context.User?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true to guard against future auth-handler changes populating claims on unauthenticated principals.
notes: Guard semantics: null-tenant (ICurrentTenant.FleetId == null) allows any explicit FleetId write — used for seeding and SuperAdmin cross-tenant writes. Non-null current tenant triggers: (1) auto-stamp when ITenantEntity.FleetId == Guid.Empty on Added entities; (2) throw InvalidOperationException when FleetId is set and mismatches the tenant (both Added and Modified). User/PushSubscription (nullable FleetId): no auto-stamp; only throw when entity FleetId is non-null and mismatches non-null tenant (both Added and Modified). Global query filters captured at context-construction time referencing ICurrentTenant.FleetId — EF Core parameterises this per-context-instance. When FleetId is null, non-nullable tenant entity queries return zero rows (fail-closed). IgnoreQueryFilters() used in tests for seeding reads. dotnet ef migrations has-pending-model-changes reports no changes — query filters do not affect the relational schema. Schema unchanged from WI-03 initial migration.
